title: Ambient module preparation for affine pieces of a finite-type morphism
statement: Let $T$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, $U\subseteq T$ a quasi-compact open, and $g:W\to T$ a finite-type morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Assume $W_U=W\times_T U\to U$ is flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-pc-fibre-product]. Then there are a finite affine open cover $W=\bigcup_{i=1}^r W_i$, integers $n_i\geq0$, quasi-compact open subschemes $V_i\subseteq\mathbb A_T^{n_i}$ [def-nagata-relative-affine-space], and closed immersions $j_i:W_i\hookrightarrow V_i$ over $T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Each $V_i\to T$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation. The $\mathcal O_{V_i}$-module $\mathcal F_i=(j_i)_*\mathcal O_{W_i}$, whose sections on an open $H\subseteq V_i$ are $\Gamma(j_i^{-1}H,\mathcal O_{W_i})$ with scalars induced by $j_i$, is quasi-coherent and of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. Its restriction to $V_i\times_T U$ is a module of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] and is flat over $U$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. The empty cover is permitted when $W$ is empty.

The immersion input is morphisms.tex, lemma-quasi-affine-finite-type-over-S; finite presentation of the quotient over the ambient algebra uses Tag 02FV, lemma-finite-presentation-permanence.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover $T=\bigcup_a B_a$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover]. By the finite-type hypothesis and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], each $g^{-1}(B_a)$ has a finite affine open cover $W_{ab}=\operatorname{Spec}C_{ab}$ with $C_{ab}$ a finitely generated algebra over $A_a=\Gamma(B_a,\mathcal O_T)$. The finitely many $W_{ab}$ cover $W$; reindex them by $i$. In particular, each $W_i$ maps into a selected affine open $B_{a(i)}$ of $T$. If $W$ is empty, take the empty family and all assertions are vacuous.

source.place: Tag 01T0, definition-finite-type; flat.tex Tag 081R, lemma-flat-after-blowing-up, finite affine covering

proof.text: For each $i$, choose algebra generators $c_1,\ldots,c_{n_i}$ of $C_i$ over $A_{a(i)}$, allowing $n_i=0$. The surjection $A_{a(i)}[t_1,\ldots,t_{n_i}]\twoheadrightarrow C_i$, $t_j\mapsto c_j$, defines a closed immersion $j_i:W_i\hookrightarrow V_i:=\operatorname{Spec}(A_{a(i)}[t_1,\ldots,t_{n_i}])$ over $B_{a(i)}$, hence over $T$, by [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The affine chart description in [def-nagata-relative-affine-space] identifies $V_i$ with the inverse image of $B_{a(i)}$ in $\mathbb A_T^{n_i}$, an open subscheme. Thus these choices give the required immersion and ambient open, with $V_i$ affine and therefore quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs].

source.place: Tag 01QO, lemma-closed-immersion; Tag 081R ambient-immersion construction in flat.tex; explicit affine-coordinate refinement

proof.text: The projection $V_i=\mathbb A_{B_{a(i)}}^{n_i}\to B_{a(i)}$ is locally of finite presentation by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The open immersion $B_{a(i)}\hookrightarrow T$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Their composite $p_i:V_i\to T$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition]. As $V_i$ is quasi-compact and $T$ is quasi-separated, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) shows $p_i$ is quasi-compact. These are the two required properties of the ambient morphism.

source.place: Tags 01TR (lemma-composition-finite-presentation), 03GI (schemes.tex lemma-quasi-compact-permanence); polynomial projection as in Tag 081R

proof.text: Set $\mathcal F_i=(j_i)_*\mathcal O_{W_i}$ with the section and scalar maps in the statement. The closed-immersion description in [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes $j_i$ affine; hence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](1) makes $\mathcal F_i$ quasi-coherent. On every affine open $H=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq V_i$, that same closed-immersion description gives $j_i^{-1}H=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ and $\mathcal F_i(H)=R/I$. This module is generated by $1$ (or is zero). By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a), $\mathcal F_i|_H$ is of finite type. Such opens cover $V_i$, so the definition gives finite type everywhere.

source.place: Tag 01QO, lemma-closed-immersion; schemes.tex lemma-push-forward-quasi-coherent; properties.tex Tag 01PB, lemma-finite-type-module

proof.text: Write $V_{i,U}=V_i\times_T U$ and $W_{i,U}=W_i\times_T U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), $V_{i,U}\to U$ is locally of finite presentation; in particular it is locally of finite type: for every affine open $V\subseteq U$, any affine open cover of the inverse image of $V$ in $V_{i,U}$ consists of affine opens whose coordinate rings are finitely presented, hence finitely generated, $\mathcal O_U(V)$-algebras by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], which is the condition of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The scheme $W_{i,U}$ is the open subscheme of $W_U$ corresponding to $W_i\subseteq W$. Its inclusion in $W_U$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale, def-weil-etale-morphism], so $W_{i,U}\to U$ is locally of finite presentation by the hypothesis on $W_U$ and [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition]. Apply [lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation] with $S=U$, $X=W_{i,U}$, $Y=V_{i,U}$: the restricted morphism $j_{i,U}$ is locally of finite presentation. It is still a closed immersion: on any affine chart the restriction is the same quotient-ring description of $j_i$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](4), $\mathcal F_i|_{V_{i,U}}=(j_{i,U})_*\mathcal O_{W_{i,U}}$. On every affine open $H=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq V_{i,U}$, the closed immersion has affine inverse image $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. By step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], $R/I$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-surjection-kernel-fg] with zero polynomial variables to $R\twoheadrightarrow R/I$. It gives $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$. Consequently $R^{m}\to R\to R/I\to0$, with first map $(r_k)\mapsto\sum_k r_k f_k$, is a finite module presentation. The quasi-coherence from step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](b) give a finite presentation of $\mathcal F_i$ on $H$. These opens cover $V_{i,U}$, proving the asserted module finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 01TV (lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation), Tag 01TQ; algebra.tex lemma-finite-presentation-independent; properties.tex Tag 01PC

proof.text: Finally apply the closed-subspace stalk formula [lem-sc-closed-pushforward-abelian-stalks] to the underlying additive sheaf of $\mathcal O_{W_{i,U}}$. Off the closed image its direct-image stalk is zero and hence flat. At $y=j_{i,U}(w)$ it is $\mathcal O_{W_{i,U},w}$. This identification is compatible with $\mathcal O_{U,u}$-scalars, where $u=p_i(y)$: a germ $a$ on $U$ acts on both sides by multiplication by its pulled-back germ at $w$, since $j_i$ is over $T$. Open subschemes have the same local rings, so this is $\mathcal O_{W_U,w}$ as an $\mathcal O_{U,u}$-module. It is flat by the assumed flatness of $W_U\to U$ and [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Thus every stalk is flat over its base local ring, exactly the stalk criterion in [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. This proves the final assertion for every $i$.
